thread.title_full: Here's the forecast for the Fleet Week air shows as S.F. weather turns rough - NewsBreak

author: Anthony Edwards
title: Here's the forecast for the Fleet Week air shows as S.F. weather turns rough - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Edwards ,
9 hours ago Spectators at Crissy Field watch the Blue Angels air show in October 2024. A foggy forecast is expected to hinder this weekend’s air show, especially on Friday. (Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle) The heat wave gripping the Bay Area is expected to break at exactly the wrong time for San Francisco’s Fleet Week air shows, which could be impacted by turbulent weather this weekend.
Fog will be most extensive Friday. The Golden Gate is expected to be blanketed in low clouds all the way through the afternoon. Poor visibility could hinder the air show from noon to 4 p.m.
Sunnier conditions are expected the rest of the weekend, but temperatures will be below normal. Gusty winds Saturday may pose danger to boaters, and there’s a slight chance of rain showers Sunday.
Here’s the Fleet Week forecast:
Foggy Friday The Blue Angels fly over the Golden Gate Bridge during Fleet Week in October 2024. The heat wave gripping the Bay Area is expected to break at the wrong time for this weekend's air shows. (Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle) Thursday will be the last day of a long-duration heat advisory for parts of the North Bay, East Bay, South Bay and Peninsula. By Friday morning, fog is expected to pour through the Golden Gate toward the Berkeley hills, the Richmond-San Rafael Bridge and the Bay Bridge.
Persistent west-southwest winds in the afternoon will continue to push fog toward Alcatraz, Angel Island and Albany. Oakland International Airport, where Fleet Week aircraft take off, is likely to be sunny.
Where fog lingers, it will be confined to the lowest 800 to 1,000 feet of the atmosphere, which should shroud the Golden Gate Bridge towers and parts of the Marin Headlands. While Oakland airport will be sunny, fog may disrupt some aircraft maneuvers over San Francisco Bay. The Blue Angels did not respond immediately to a request for an update Thursday morning, but a pared-down show seems possible.
The Blue Angels must have a minimum cloud ceiling of 10,000 feet and visibility of 3 miles to perform their unrestricted “high show,” which includes all of the maneuvers, according to the U.S. Navy . They can still perform a “flat show” with limited maneuvers, even when the cloud ceiling is 1,500 feet, which the Federal Aviation Administration can waive to 1,000 feet. With a 4,500-foot cloud ceiling, some rolling maneuvers can be performed in a “low show.”
People hoping to watch the air show from the water may not be able to see the sky above. Winds of 15 to 25 mph (up to 20 knots) are also expected from the Golden Gate to Treasure Island to Point Richmond. Temperatures on the water will be in the low 60s.
Coit Tower, the Embarcadero and Tiburon will probably be the best places for clear skies with fog in the distance. Crissy Field and Fisherman’s Wharf are expected to go in and out of the fog. Temperatures in the city will be in the low to mid-60s, with 70-degree readings in sunny parts of Marin County.
Windy Saturday Increasing winds Saturday will be strong enough to whisk away the fog, but the blustery conditions will present other hazards.
Westerly winds will gust up to 30 mph (25 knots) through the Golden Gate, with wave heights of 1 to 2 feet around Alcatraz. Conditions will be even worse on the outer coastal waters, gale-force winds and very rough seas.
Gusts of 20 to 30 wouldn’t be unusual by midsummer standards, but October is typically one of the calmest months of the year along San Francisco Bay. In July, a vessel sank near Alcatraz Island on a windy day. Three people died, and another is presumed dead.
Earlier this year, the Blue Angels canceled a performance in Seattle when wind speeds were 15 mph, according to the Seattle Times . It is not clear whether similar conditions would impact a performance at Fleet Week.
Weather wild card Sunday Sunday’s forecast is trickier.
Wind will diminish, but three separate weather systems will merge over California, including the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. Slight deviations in the placements in any of these systems will impact the forecast.
Anything from isolated showers to abundant sunshine is possible. Rain and clouds are most likely if the systems remain just off the coast, while dry weather will prevail from a farther east track. Sunny weather is most likely, but it’s worth keeping an eye on the forecast just in case.
Regardless, Bay Area temperatures will be below normal, in the 60s near the water, with occasional breezes making for light jacket weather.
